mechanism: Measurement only, no library change. A new example, examples/crossbred_m3_bench.rs, runs the same targets through every m=3 Koblitz K_0 decomposition oracle as the pipeline calls them: PairSumTable::decompose (the production default), enumerate_decompose (the reference verdict), groebner_decompose with InheritedF4{3} and with MatrixF4{3}, and crossbred_decompose with the production params (k=v/2 capped at 22) and with a tuned (D,k) (the smallest k with kernel_dim >= v-k). An optional root level compares the full Boolean root sets. Groebner stops at the first root that lifts; crossbred solves the whole system before lifting. That is why crossbred loses on cells that decompose and wins only on overdetermined cells with no decomposition.
prediction: Written before measuring: verdicts agree, and production crossbred may return Unknown at n>=9. At n=9, InheritedF4 costs 20-130M bit ops and tuned crossbred about 30M (within 3x either way); MatrixF4 is at least 10x crossbred. At n=15, crossbred uses 2-5x fewer bit ops than InheritedF4 (about 0.4G). Pair table is at least 1000x faster in wall time everywhere. Outcome: verdict agreement confirmed. The crossbred n=9 figure was right (30.3M). The 3x band failed on native ops (11.7x worse) and held on native+aux (1.14x). MatrixF4 >= 10x was falsified (17.5M vs 30.3M). The n=15 InheritedF4 guess was falsified (11.7M), and the crossbred advantage was smaller than predicted (1.16x at n=15, 3.3x at n=31). The 1000x bound was falsified: pair table was 40-6800x faster, but it won every cell.

indicative_timing: Indicative only, shared VM. Wall ms per target, pair table / InheritedF4 / tuned crossbred: n9 0.013 / 1.03 / 71.3; n13 0.181 (plus a 377 ms one-time table build) / 7.5 / 7266 (Unknown); n15 0.006 / 1.74 / 1.87; n31 0.009 / 61.1 / 88.1. MatrixF4 takes 162 s and production crossbred 343 s per target at n=31. Crossbred is slower in wall time than InheritedF4 at every cell, including n=31 where its native counter is 3.3x lower.
risks: The F4 and crossbred native counters count different inner loops, and at n=31 wall time contradicts the bit-op ranking. Cells have few targets (6-12). n=7 and n=15 are degenerate (|F|=1, all "no"). n=11, 17 and 21 have no K_0 curve, and n=31 has no "yes" cells. Only m=3 on K_0 was measured. Crossbred extraction ops are counted by a second, deterministic extraction in the harness. MatrixF4 and production crossbred at n=31 were run on 1 target. Possible future lead, not a default change: DecompositionStrategy::Crossbred with default params (k=v/2) is badly tuned, and picking the smallest k with kernel_dim >= v-k is up to 8000x cheaper.
